title: How to (Accidentally) Read the Baku Marriage Market. Tip #1
body: She is 25 and the questions have started, at every gathering, from people who have no other material. Nobody asks the men. The men are asked what they do. She is asked when. It's a sealed deal if she has a prepared answer she has now used eleven times and delivers with a smile that does not move.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 elçilik season is undefeated.

title: How to (Accidentally) Read the Baku Marriage Market. Tip #2
body: Watch the elçilik machinery, because it starts long before anyone visits. Somebody's mother knows somebody's aunt. There has been research. Someone has looked at an Instagram profile very carefully and reported back to a committee. By the time tea is poured, both families know more about each other than either will admit. It's a sealed deal if a relative has produced a photograph on a phone and said only "bax."
caption:
Tip #2 😭 elçilik season is undefeated.

title: How to (Accidentally) Read the Baku Marriage Market. Tip #3
body: Listen to what is actually being asked in the first ten minutes. Not the words. The words are about the weather and the traffic. The information being gathered is: family, work, flat or no flat, and whether the mother is difficult. Everybody is running the same audit at the same time. It's a sealed deal if the tea is poured by the youngest person present and everyone watched how she did it.
caption:
Tip #3 😭 elçilik season is undefeated.

title: How to (Accidentally) Read the Baku Marriage Market. Tip #4
body: Ask about the flat, because it decides more than anyone will say. Whether the couple will live with his parents is the single biggest question in the entire negotiation, and it gets discussed in code for weeks. "Ayrı" means one thing. Silence means another. It's a sealed deal if a whole family has argued for a month about a two-bedroom in a building that is not finished.
caption:
Tip #4 😭 elçilik season is undefeated.

title: How to (Accidentally) Read the Baku Marriage Market. Tip #5
body: Watch the age gap between the sisters, because it is a timer. Traditionally the older one goes first, and if she is 29 and the younger one has a serious situation, the whole family is now in a quiet negotiation nobody named. Both sisters are aware. Neither will raise it. It's a sealed deal if the younger one has slowed down her own plans for a year and never once said why.
caption:
Tip #5 😭 elçilik season is undefeated.

title: How to (Accidentally) Read the Baku Marriage Market. Tip #6
body: Ask what she's actually looking for and see how quickly the honest answer arrives. Not the list she gives relatives. The real one is usually two things: someone whose mother she can survive, and someone who will not be embarrassed by her job. It's a sealed deal if she has turned down someone perfectly acceptable over one sentence he said about her working.
caption:
Tip #6 😭 elçilik season is undefeated.

title: How to (Accidentally) Read the Baku Marriage Market. Tip #7
body: Watch the cousins' group chat, because that is where the actual decisions get made. The parents think they are running this. The cousins have already vetoed two candidates and promoted one. Information moves faster there than in the entire elçilik apparatus. It's a sealed deal if a proposal has been quietly ended by a screenshot.
caption:
Tip #7 😭 elçilik season is undefeated.
